To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) We identified a set of words that can be used as indicators of changes in the postpartum period.

(i) childbirth is associated with changes in the posting patterns and emotional expression of most new mothers, (ii) these changes are more significant in 15% of the new mothers, and (iii) these mothers can be characterized by shifts in a small number of words.

we find that 15% of mothers exhibit significant changes in online behavior and emotion expression postpartum; that we can characterize these changes in terms of a small set of linguistic features; and that we can predict the type of changes in these features that are associated with postpartum depression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how social media data can be leveraged for the purpose of identifying and understanding the dynamics of major life changes and behavioral shifts.
the identification of significant changes in the language of mothers following childbirth, and their potential use in characterizing postpartum well-being.
the use of social media as an indicator of changes in the lives of people and populations.

we have developed and validated a method for identifying and characterizing significant changes in women’s emotional and linguistic expression in social media around the time of childbirth.
the study of social media is a useful tool for understanding the dynamics of major life events in the population.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the majority of mothers do not show significant changes in social media posting patterns or emotional expression after childbirth, and that a small number of mothers show changes that are associated with a shift in the type of language they use in social media posts.

the social media activity and language of women who experience significant changes in the postnatal period can be distinguished from those who do not, suggesting that social media can be a useful tool for understanding the postnatal course of new mothers and for identifying mothers at risk of postpartum depression.
social media can be harnessed to understand the dynamics of major life events, and to identify individuals with significant changes in their behavior following such events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to identify significant behavioral changes in social media following childbirth.

the language used in social media posts can provide a window into the emotional and behavioral changes that occur in women following childbirth, and that this window can help us identify a subset of women that are at risk of developing postnatal depression.
social media can provide a unique window on the lives of individuals, and that the language of these individuals can be leveraged to understand and predict their health and well-being.
